triggerReasons.message: High-risk or gate/security wording selects high-assurance intent hardening.
High-assurance work requires an independent intent-collision result.
Ambiguity, user impact, behavior change, or multi-deliverable intent makes intent collision diagnostically required.
Bug, regression, security/auth/session, benchmark, or explicit behavior-change work should have red evidence.
Broad or absolute scope wording should have scope clarification before future enforcement.

acceptanceBindings.note: The acceptance claim is a single observable command output, so its primary binding is the CLI item plus the planner item that produces the tier decision and the glossed reason codes the output prints. CHK-004:happy:1 is included because the claim requires every escalation reason to be followed by a plain-language gloss, which is asserted by enumerating the reason-code enum rather than by a hand-copied list.

The second half of the acceptance claim is that the story store is byte-identical before and after the call. That is bound to the adversarial store-snapshot fixture and to the command-policy readOnly classification, so the prose guarantee and the mechanical classification are both required to hold.

The claim that ids do not come from label or position is bound to the position-invariance and label-rename fixtures, plus the adversarial fixture proving the existing routine identity digest is unperturbed while declaring an id does change source.inputDigest. The label-rename case carries both halves at once: the id survives and the commandSetDigest changes.

The claim that each pin resolves to exactly one real command is bound to both positive resolution paths and to both stop paths. The adversarial ambiguity fixture is what makes exactly-one meaningful: without it, a first-match resolver would satisfy the positive cases alone.

The claim that the operator sees which Story inputs were collected is bound to the collector's positive case and to the three cases where a naive implementation would silently under-report: rename and delete seeds, canonical material exclusion, and a failed changed-file read that must escalate rather than read as no changes.

Every binding above is only worth its fixture if that fixture actually runs, so the whole acceptance surface is additionally bound to registration in the canonical membership authority plus its separate resource policy mapping, to the RED-before-GREEN commit ordering check, and to the zod-bypass rejection fixtures required by the handler encoding convention.

diagnosticGaps.message: Red evidence is triggered but no current red evidence record binds baseline head/material to the correct acceptance target and green relation.

note: Bindings map the original intent snapshot's single acceptance claim onto the checklist and verification intents that mechanically prove it. Written at PLAN before implementation. The claim is deliberately about what an operator can OBSERVE from one command invocation, not about internal structure, because this Story's user-visible value is the explain output and the read-only guarantee; the identity, pin and collector items are bound as the facts that output asserts.
